Service operations · Platform in use

Luxflow

I run a UK fulfilment business for online sellers. I planned how an order should move from a seller’s shipping label to a packed parcel, and what the warehouse and seller each need to see along the way.

What happens when an order arrives

The seller uploads a shipping label and lists the items in the parcel. Once they submit the order, the portal records it, deducts each item from stock and calculates the fulfilment charge. I still check the items, pack the parcel and mark the order complete.

Part-deliveries raised a different problem. If a seller cancels the outstanding units after some stock has arrived, the warehouse still needs a record of what it received. I specified that rule for the portal and coordinated its development. The released cancellation workflow keeps received quantities on record when the outstanding delivery is closed.

WhatsApp support assistant · test stage

For a separate support assistant, I considered which enquiries I could delegate and which needed my judgement. A routine question about our fulfilment service can be answered from approved business information. A request for a custom price, a complaint or a report of missing stock goes into the owner’s “Needs Me” queue. Taking over a chat pauses automatic replies for that conversation.

What the test showed

An incoming message reached the dashboard on a WhatsApp test number. An automatic reply and a reply sent manually were both marked as read. The trial used one verified recipient on a test number. It established that messages could pass in both directions. Using the assistant with customers and evaluating their experience would require a separate trial.

For future research, I am interested in what happens to a customer’s trust when a business explains why their question has been passed from an assistant to a person.
